D014_l001.question:

There is marked lack of self-assurance, with frequent self-doubt regarding clinical decisions at work and daily choices outside the workplace, despite adequate training and performance feedback. A pervasive cognitive style of chronic pessimism is noted, with automatic negative interpretations of events and difficulty recognizing potential positive outcomes.  

Symptoms have been continuously present without remission exceeding two months at any point during the course. There is evidence of functional impairment, particularly in work performance and social engagement, though the patient maintains employment. No acute psychotic features, manic episodes, or recent substance use are reported. The clinical picture is consistent with a chronic, low-grade depressive disorder with early onset and sustained duration, significantly affecting quality of life and adaptive functioning. Psychosocial stressors are minimal, and a history of major life events—including her parents’ divorce five years ago—predates symptom onset by a considerable interval.
